title: All-sky Search for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Isolated Neutron Stars in the First Part of the Fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Observing Run
extended_summary:
This paper reports an astrophysical search for continuous gravitational waves from isolated neutron stars using the first eight months of LIGO data from the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run. The central problem is whether nearly monochromatic gravitational-wave signals can be detected in all-sky data and, if not, what upper limits can be placed on source strain and related astrophysical quantities.

The study evaluates three search pipelines: PowerFlux, FrequencyHough, and SOAP. PowerFlux and FrequencyHough are semi-coherent template-based methods, while SOAP is a more model-agnostic Viterbi-based search augmented with convolutional neural network follow-up. The analysis spans roughly 20–2000 Hz and includes a wide range of frequency derivatives, with hardware injections used to validate the pipelines and outlier follow-up procedures.

No credible continuous-wave signal was detected. The paper instead reports 95% confidence upper limits on strain amplitude and uses them to constrain several astrophysical scenarios, including the Galactic population of highly deformed neutron stars, the millisecond pulsar explanation for the Galactic Center GeV excess, and possible contributions from asteroid-mass primordial black-hole binaries. The conclusions are negative-detection results plus astrophysical constraints rather than an intervention study.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is an astrophysics/gravitational-wave search, not an education study, and it contains no K-12 intervention, comparator, or learner outcome evidence. There is no relevant methodology for the requested taxonomy beyond the publication being a peer-reviewed research article.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no educational impact because the paper does not evaluate any educational technology or student outcome. It is irrelevant to the requested K-12 science AI comparison evidence base.
